headline: ZIJIN KILLS ALLIED GOLD ACQUISITION, TAKES $295M MINORITY STAKE INSTEAD — 9.2% at C$32.55 Closes ~Aug 10; Deal Collapsed on Conditions Deadline (NYSE/TSX: AAUC)
snippet: Allied Gold Corporation announced July 29 that its arrangement agreement with Zijin Gold International has been terminated — both parties concluded conditions could not be fulfilled by the July 29 outside date or within any reasonable time thereafter. Rather than walking away, Zijin Gold simultaneously agreed to a US$295 million strategic minority investment, subscribing for approximately 12.8 million Allied Gold common shares at C$32.55 per share (the 30-day VWAP as of July 27, representing a premium to the current trading price) for a ~9.2% stake expected to close around August 10. For retail investors: the full-acquisition thesis is dead, but Zijin remains Allied's largest single shareholder — a Chinese strategic vote of confidence in African gold production at a price Zijin itself set in writing.

headline: FIRST QUANTUM Q2: COPPER SURGES 10% TO 100,487 TONNES — Net Earnings Jump $18M to $136M Year-on-Year; Sentinel and Kansanshi Both Deliver (TSX: FM)
snippet: First Quantum Minerals reported Q2 2026 copper production of 100,487 tonnes — up 10.3% from the 91,069 tonnes produced in Q2 2025 — as both Sentinel and Kansanshi in Zambia outperformed. Net earnings attributable to shareholders surged from US$18 million to US$136 million year-over-year; revenue rose to US$1.5 billion from US$1.22 billion. Gross profit was US$297 million and EBITDA US$400 million. The company flagged stronger second-half production visibility as Kansanshi's S3 circuit continues to ramp and Sentinel's debottlenecking program progresses — with Cobre Panamá stockpiles still available to process if political conditions allow.

headline: G MINING VENTURES CLOSES G2 GOLDFIELDS DEAL TODAY — G3 Goldfields Spun Out; Guyana Gold Consolidated Under One Operator (TSX: GMIN)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / G Mining Ventures
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) announced July 29 the successful closing of its acquisition of all issued and outstanding shares of G2 Goldfields under the Canada Business Corporations Act plan of arrangement. Holders of G2 shares received 0.212 of a GMIN share plus 0.5 of a G3 Goldfields share for each G2 share held. G3 Goldfields, which now trades separately, holds the exploration-stage assets from the G2 portfolio. The transaction consolidates two Guyana gold operations and creates a single acquirer with greater balance sheet depth and potential access to capital markets at scale — a model for the mid-tier consolidation wave that analysts have predicted will characterise the second half of 2026.

headline: EMPEROR METALS HITS 21.3m @ 3.0 g/t AU AT 45m DEPTH — Near-Surface Grade Supports Open-Pit PEA Case at Duquesne West, Quebec (CSE: AUOZ)
snippet: Emperor Metals Inc. (CSE: AUOZ) released July 29 the latest assay batch from its ongoing 2026 campaign at the Duquesne West Project in Quebec's Abitibi Gold Belt, with drill hole DQ26-43 intersecting 21.3 metres grading 3.0 g/t gold from a downhole depth of 64.9 metres — estimated at only 45 metres vertical depth. The result is part of an integrated dataset now exceeding 135,000 metres of total drilling across the property, combining new 2026 holes with 8,000 metres of resampled historical core. The consistent near-surface high-grade intercepts are directional evidence for a potential open-pit mining scenario that would underpin the Preliminary Economic Assessment the company is targeting in the near term.

headline: URZ3 ENERGY ADDS 10,900 ACRES TO WYOMING URANIUM ISR PORTFOLIO — Three State Leases + 437 New Claims in Powder River Basin; DOE Supply Sourcing in Focus (TSXV: URZ)
snippet: URZ3 Energy Corp. (TSXV: URZ) announced July 29 the acquisition of three Wyoming state mineral leases covering approximately 1,920 acres and 437 unpatented mining claims covering approximately 9,000 acres — expanding its Powder River Basin uranium position by roughly 10,900 acres. The targets are sandstone-hosted ISR-amenable uranium trends consistent with the Dry Fork Project geology. Wyoming's Powder River Basin is one of the highest-priority domestic uranium supply corridors identified under the US Department of Energy's 2026 critical minerals sourcing framework, and ISR methods offer a lower capital path to production than conventional open-pit mining.

headline: BANYAN GOLD FINDS HIGH-GRADE AT TWO NEW NITRA ZONES — Roaring Fork and Seattle Creek Both Hit in First Exploration Holes; 830 sq km District No-Royalty Land (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced July 28 that the first two exploration drill holes at the Nitra Gold Project in Yukon's Mayo Mining District have each returned visible gold and high-grade mineralization — hitting within the newly identified Roaring Fork zone and Seattle Creek zone respectively. These are the first of eleven exploration targets identified across Banyan's 830 sq km combined AurMac-Nitra land package, 100% owned with no underlying royalties and located approximately 25 km west of the AurMac Deposit. Assays are pending from a fully funded 7,500-metre, two-rig program. If Nitra delivers results that parallel AurMac, Banyan's district-scale thesis gets substantially more expensive to replicate.

headline: FIRST DRILL BIT EVER IN ISLE AUX MORTS GRANITE — AuMEGA Launches 10,000m Cape Ray Discovery Hunt at Two Never-Before-Tested Targets, Newfoundland (TSX/ASX: AUM)
snippet: AuMEGA Metals Inc. (TSX/ASX: AUM, OTCQB: AUMMF) announced July 28 the commencement of its largest-ever, fully funded 2026 drill program, with diamond drilling now underway at the Isle aux Morts Granite and Cape Ray West along the Cape Ray Shear Zone in Newfoundland and Labrador — two target areas that have never previously been drilled. Structural, geochemical, and geophysical targets from systematic regional mapping informed hole placement; drilling will advance to the Bunker Hill target following completion of these initial holes. AuMEGA's program is targeting approximately 10,000 metres of resource growth and greenfield discovery drilling through the summer of 2026.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH INDEX STAYS NEAR 272 — NdPr Alloy Hits New 2026 High Above $137/kg; Heavy Rare Earths Tighten as MOFCOM Locks Western Buyers Out
snippet: China's Rare Earth Price Index held near 272 in the week ending July 28, 2026 — 172% above its 2010 baseline — as NdPr alloy benchmarks rose to US$137–141/kg, establishing a new 2026 high above the March peak of $126/kg. Dysprosium oxide quoted at US$210–217/kg and terbium oxide at approximately US$1,034–1,043/kg, with both heavy rare earths difficult to source outside Asia at commercial volumes. The pricing backdrop reflects a tightening driven by two factors: China's Ministry of Commerce in June added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control list, restricting any entity globally from supplying China-origin dual-use items to them; and EV and wind turbine demand continues to run ahead of Western supply expansion timelines. For junior rare earth developers, the pricing context is the most favourable since mid-2022.

headline: SANKAMAP'S KUMA PORPHYRY HOLE REACHES 840m — Multi-Zone Alteration Confirmed Through Solomon Islands Copper-Gold System; Scale Still Unresolved (CSE: SCU)
snippet: Sankamap Metals Inc. (CSE: SCU) announced July 29 that drilling has resumed at its 4,500-hectare Kuma Property in the Solomon Islands after a planned technical pause to integrate early geological observations into the targeting model. Drill hole KU26-001 has advanced to 840 metres depth, intersecting multiple zones of mineralisation and alteration between 250 and 840 metres — consistent with the broad footprint of a large-scale hydrothermal system. The fully funded 2,000–3,000 metre program is testing a 2-kilometre-long lithocap above what the company believes is a significant copper-gold porphyry. First assays are pending; at 840 metres with multiple alteration zones encountered, the system is proving deeper than many early-stage Pacific porphyry programs.

headline: SILVER HOLDS $57 BUT FACES TWO TESTS IN 48 HOURS — Hawkish Fed Raised PCE Forecast Today; Thursday's Core PCE Print Is the Next Binary for the Bull Case
snippet: Following the July 29 FOMC decision, the Federal Reserve's upward revision to its 2026 Core PCE inflation forecast — paired with the projection of just one rate cut for the year — sent silver lower from the $57.40 area, though the metal held above its near-term $57 structural support. Thursday at 8:30 a.m. ET delivers the actual June PCE print: a soft number could trigger the relief rally that silver bulls have been waiting for since the metal printed an 8-month low of $55.50 on July 17; a hot print validates the hawkish revised forecasts and could push silver back toward that low. The structural backdrop remains intact — the Silver Institute projects a 46.3 million-ounce supply deficit in 2026, the sixth consecutive year of structural undersupply — but macro timing is doing most of the price work in the near term.
